paper_metadata.title: Statistics-informed parameterized quantum circuit: towards practical quantum state preparation and learning via maximum entropy principle

summary: The paper introduces a statistics‑informed parameterized quantum circuit (SI‑PQC) for quantum state preparation using the maximum entropy principle. Numerical simulations on a noiseless QPanda statevector simulator show preparation of several distributions (Gaussian, exponential, chi‑squared, Rayleigh), a 4‑component Gaussian mixture, and a variational learning example recovering μ1=6, μ2=14 and σ1²=16, σ2²=22.5. Resource analysis suggests asymptotic depth O(n M df log(1/ε)/F) for distribution loading and improved scaling for mixture preparation compared with naive LCU methods.

experiments.description: Maximum Entropy Distribution Loader (MEDL) for preparing single statistical distributions (exponential, chi-squared, normal/Gaussian, and Rayleigh) on a gate-based quantum simulator.

algorithm.variant: Statistics-Informed Parameterized Quantum Circuit (SI-PQC) / Maximum Entropy Distribution Loader (MEDL)
algorithm.ansatz: fixed-structure SI-PQC with state-preparation-pair and QSVT-based imaginary-time evolution
algorithm.parameter_initialization: perfect prior knowledge of distribution law and parameters; rotation angles computed analytically from model parameters

problem_formulation.encoding_details: n = ceil(log2 N) qubits for N discretization points; amplitudes encode discretized probability amplitudes p(x)=sqrt(P(x))
problem_formulation.objective_function: prepare |p⟩ = sum_x (1/N) exp(sum_k λ_k f_k(x)) |x⟩ for a target distribution
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: maximum entropy principle with observables as constraints; no penalty formulation

problem_instance.description: Prepare four representative distribution families with multiple parameter settings; numerical experiments shown for chi-squared, exponential, normal, and Rayleigh distributions

dataset_specification.description: discretized distributions on equally spaced points; parameter sets include k=2,4,6 for chi-squared, λ=0.2,0.5,1.0 for exponential, μ/σ settings for normal, and σ^2=64,144,256 for Rayleigh

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: compare experimental scatter points against theoretical discretization curves

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: compare measured amplitudes/probabilities to theoretical discretization

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: sliding window of length 1000; incremental update of monitored expectations; use E[X] and E[ln X] as conservative constraints while E[X^2] varies strongly
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: compare quantum VaR estimates against empirical VaR at α=0.95, 0.85, 0.05 over timestamps grouped by 100
